entities.summary:
Marvel Comics, a leading publisher of comic books and related media, has been a significant force in the North American entertainment industry since its founding in 1961. 

As a major player in the development of the modern comic book industry, Marvel Comics has played a crucial role in shaping popular culture, with iconic characters such as Spider-Man, the X-Men, and the Avengers. 

The company's influence can be seen in the many films, television shows, and video games that have been based on its characters, with Marvel's Cinematic Universe (MCU) being one of the most successful and lucrative in the industry. 

Marvel Comics' legacy extends beyond its entertainment products, as it has also been a major driver of social change, with its characters serving as role models for diverse audiences and promoting messages of inclusivity and representation. 

In 2013, Marvel Comics was acquired by The Walt Disney Company, cementing its position as a global entertainment powerhouse. 

In the end, Marvel Comics' impact on popular culture and society is undeniable, with its characters and stories continuing to inspire new generations of fans and creators alike.
